newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee stagnates, eyes downside.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee stagnates, eyes downside.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee stagnated in directionless early trade and dealers said they expected the unit to come under downward pressure against the dollar.
The rupee, which was untraded nearly two hours after opening, was quoted at its previous closing rate of 57.14 at 0400 GMT.
"There is no possibility of an upward movement because the exchange rate is already at the Central Bank top," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
The Central Bank buying and selling prices were unchanged at 56.0241 and 57.1559 for the second day indicating that the authorities were comfortable with the current exchange rate, dealers said.
A Sampath Bank dealer said there would be little activity in the forex market with most banks covering imports with dollars from the Central Bank.
Overnight call money was down at 14.5 percent after opening at 15.5, due to a number of non-banking lenders in the market, he said.
